title: Knight Riders Group Eyes The Hundred Entry as Expansion to Ten Teams Gains Momentum
excerpt: Having passed on buying existing franchises, KKR's owners could target a new team if the ECB adds ninth and tenth franchises — a move league officials have called a 'no-brainer.'
body:
• The Knight Riders Group, which owns franchises in the IPL, CPL, MLC, and a newly acquired UAE T20 league team, declined to buy existing Hundred teams but could enter through expansion
  • ECB officials have described adding ninth and tenth teams as a "no-brainer," with Durham and Bristol as likely host cities
  • Current Hundred investors hold a veto on expansion, meaning any new teams would require buy-in from existing franchise owners — including Indian-owned rivals

When the ECB put stakes in its eight Hundred teams up for sale in 2025, the Knight Riders Group — the Shah Rukh Khan-led entity behind Kolkata Knight Riders, Trinbago Knight Riders, Los Angeles Knight Riders, and now Abu Dhabi Knight Riders — was conspicuous in its restraint. The group evaluated the opportunity but ultimately decided the business model was not viable for existing franchises, according to Cricbuzz, which reported that KKR viewed the acquisition as "an unviable proposition, businesswise."

The Expansion Opportunity

That calculus could change if the Hundred expands. Vikram Banerjee, the ECB's director of business operations, has publicly stated that adding ninth and tenth teams is a "no-brainer." Speculation has centered on Durham and Bristol as the most likely host cities, given their existing credentials as international cricket venues, according to a Brabners analysis of the competition's financial structure.

https://x.com/SportsbyHT/status/2089304503329939809

For the Knight Riders Group, a brand-new franchise in an expanded Hundred would solve several problems that made existing teams unattractive. A new team would come without legacy obligations, existing player contracts, or joint-venture complexities with established county cricket clubs. It would also be priced based on projected rather than historical value — a distinction that matters for a group that questioned the ECB's broadcast revenue projections for the 2029-32 cycle.

"We think about it for the long haul. If it has to work, then the people, the chemistry has to be a big determining factor."

— Venky Mysore, CEO of Knight Riders Group, to ESPNcricinfo

A Global Franchise Empire

The Knight Riders have been among the most aggressive franchise builders in world cricket. Their latest acquisition — Abu Dhabi Knight Riders in the UAE's upcoming T20 league — was announced in August 2026, alongside fellow franchise owners including Mukesh Ambani's Reliance, Gautam Adani's Adani Group, and the Glazer family. The six-team UAE league is expected to launch early next year, according to Cricbuzz.

KKR CEO Venky Mysore told ESPNcricinfo that the group prioritizes "chemistry" with local partners over pure financial transactions. "Like in any joint venture there are legacy issues which will be there in the Hundred, too," he said. "The existing shareholder group has existed for 100-plus years, and suddenly, you have a new investor coming in."

The Veto Problem

There is a significant structural barrier. Current Hundred investors secured a veto on any expansion during their purchase negotiations, as reported by The Observer. That means adding a ninth or tenth team would require the agreement of existing franchise owners — several of whom are rival IPL entities, including Reliance (MI London), Sun Group (Sunrisers Leeds), and GMR Group (Southern Brave).

Whether these owners would welcome a Knight Riders-branded competitor into an already crowded market is an open question. The IPL's own expansion from eight to ten teams in 2022 generated massive windfall fees, but also diluted the player pool and competitive balance. Similar concerns would apply to the Hundred.

When, Not If

For the Knight Riders, the Hundred represents the most significant gap in their global portfolio. They operate in the Caribbean, the United States, the UAE, and India — but not in the country where cricket began. If expansion happens before the next broadcast cycle in 2029, expect the Knight Riders to be among the first callers. The question is whether the existing owners will open the door.
